main_issue: Whether and how Agent D may keep cooking strong-smelling fish curry in the shared kitchen given smell complaints from A, B and C

A-B.evidence: Both complain about smell (turns 1-2) and both accept weekends-only with a warning (turns 10, 13); they never address each other directly.

A-C.evidence: Both complain about smell (turns 1, 3) and both accept the weekend deal (turns 11, 13); no direct exchange.

A-D.evidence: A first asked for no strong-smelling cooking at all (turn 1 setup) and D offered weekend/warning (turn 4). A said the weekend is better, though warning alone is not enough (turn 5). D agreed to weekends plus a warning (turn 12) and A said 'sounds good' (turn 13).

B-C.evidence: Both raised smell complaints (turns 2-3) and both accepted weekends (turns 10-11); no direct exchange.

B-D.evidence: B asked for a weekend plus a heads-up (turn 8) and D agreed to both (turn 9). B said 'that works for me' (turn 10) and D confirmed the settlement (turn 12).

C-D.evidence: D asked whether the plan works for C's laundry (turn 9). C replied 'weekend is fine for me' (turn 11) and D confirmed it was settled (turn 12).
